title: Scatter Plots and Lines of Best Fit
seo_title: Grade 8 Scatter Plots Worksheets: Association, Outliers, Line of Best Fit and Predictions
standard_text: Construct and interpret scatter plots for bivariate measurement data to investigate patterns of association between two quantities. Describe patterns such as clustering, outliers, positive or negative association, linear association, and nonlinear association.
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 scatter plot worksheets: describe positive, negative and no association, linear or nonlinear patterns, find outliers and clusters, judge a line of best fit, and use its equation to predict. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Points going up show positive association; going down, negative; no pattern, none.
key_sub: A line of best fit follows the trend. Use its equation to predict, and read its slope as a rate.
body_html:
Scatter plots

A scatter plot shows pairs of numbers as points. It helps you see if two variables are related.

PatternMeaning
Points go uppositive association
Points go downnegative association
No patternno association
Points follow a curvenonlinear association

Line of best fit

A straight line close to most points, with about as many above as below. Its slope is the change in y for each 1 in x. Its y-intercept is the predicted y when x = 0.

Example

A line of best fit is y = 5x + 60 (x = hours studied, y = score). Predict the score for 6 hours.

y = 5(6) + 60 = 30 + 60.

Answer: 90

Common mistakes

  • Saying a weak trend is no association.
  • Thinking association means cause.
  • Drawing the line through the first and last points only.
  • Predicting far outside the data.

faq.q: What does a scatter plot show?
faq.a: It shows pairs of data as points so you can see if two variables are related: positive, negative or no association.

faq.q: How do you draw a line of best fit?
faq.a: Draw a straight line that follows the trend, close to most points, with about as many points above it as below it.

faq.q: What is an outlier in a scatter plot?
faq.a: A point that is far away from the pattern of the other points.

faq.q: Does a strong association mean one thing causes the other?
faq.a: No. Two things can be related because of a third factor. Association is not cause.

items.q: What kind of association does the scatter plot show?
items.e: As x goes up, y tends to go up. Positive association.

items.q: What kind of association does the scatter plot show?
items.e: As x goes up, y tends to go down. Negative association.

items.q: What kind of association does the scatter plot show?
items.e: The points are spread out with no up or down pattern. No association.

items.q: A scatter plot shows that people who sleep more tend to make fewer mistakes. What kind of association is it?
items.e: More sleep goes with fewer mistakes: one goes up as the other goes down. Negative association.

items.q: What kind of association does the scatter plot show?
items.e: The points rise together closely. Positive association.

items.q: Is the association linear or nonlinear?
items.e: The points follow a curve, not a straight line. Nonlinear.

items.q: What kind of association does the scatter plot show?
items.e: The trend is weak, but y still tends to go down as x goes up. Negative association.

items.q: Taller trees tend to have wider trunks. What kind of association is it?
items.e: Both go up together: Positive association.

items.q: What kind of association does the scatter plot show?
items.e: Warmer days go with more sales. Positive association.

items.q: Is the association linear or nonlinear?
items.e: The points lie close to a straight line. Linear.

items.q: What kind of association does the scatter plot show?
items.e: Older cars tend to be worth less. Negative association.

items.q: Ice cream sales and sunburns both go up in summer. Does eating ice cream cause sunburn?
c: No, both are linked to hot weather
items.e: Association does not prove cause. No, both are linked to hot weather.

items.q: What kind of association does the scatter plot show?
items.e: There is no pattern. No association.

items.q: Is the association linear or nonlinear?
items.e: The points go down along a rough straight line. Linear.

items.q: What kind of association does the scatter plot show?

items.q: A strong association means the points …
c: lie close to a line or curve
items.e: Strong means the points lie close to a line or curve.

items.q: What kind of association does the scatter plot show?
items.e: More absences tend to go with lower grades, though the points are spread. Negative association.

items.q: Is the association linear or nonlinear?
items.e: The points go down and then up: a curve. Nonlinear.

items.q: What kind of association does the scatter plot show?
items.e: Older children tend to be taller. Positive association.

items.q: What kind of association does the scatter plot show?
items.e: Higher up tends to be colder. Negative association.

items.q: Which point is an outlier?
items.e: An outlier is far from the other points. The point near (9, 1) does not follow the pattern.

items.q: Should a line of best fit go through the outlier?
c: No, it should follow the main pattern
Only if the outlier is high
It must start at the outlier
items.e: The line shows the trend of most points: no, it should follow the main pattern.

items.q: Points are spread out with no pattern. Can you draw a useful line of best fit?
items.e: With no pattern, a line does not help: no, there is no association.

items.q: Which point is an outlier?
items.e: An outlier is far from the other points. The point near (9, 9) does not follow the pattern.

items.q: How many points should be above and below a good line of best fit?
items.e: A good line has about the same number of points on each side.

items.q: Which point is an outlier?

items.q: A line of best fit for a negative association has a …
items.e: Going down from left to right means a negative slope.

items.q: Which point is an outlier?

items.e: It should be close to most points.

items.q: Which point is an outlier?

items.q: Two scatter plots both go up. In which is the association stronger?
c: The one with points closer to a line
items.e: Strength is how close the points are to a line: the one with points closer to a line.

items.q: Most points rise, but a few at the right go down a lot. What might you see?
items.e: Rising then falling is a curve: a nonlinear pattern.

items.q: A scatter plot compares two …
c: sets of numbers about the same things
items.e: Each point pairs two measurements: sets of numbers about the same things.

items.q: Why do we make a scatter plot?
c: To see if two variables are related
To show parts of a whole
items.e: A scatter plot shows if two variables are related.

items.q: A line of best fit is y = 5x + 60, where x is hours studied and y is test score. Predict y when x = 6.
items.e: Put x = 6 in: 5(6) + 60. So about 90 points.

items.q: The line of best fit is y = 5x + 60 (x = hours studied, y = test score). What does the slope mean?
c: Each extra hour of study adds about 5 points
A student who studies 0 hours scores 5
items.e: The slope 5 is the change in score for each hour: each extra hour of study adds about 5 points.

items.q: A line of best fit is y = 2.5x + 10, where x is age (years) and y is height (in.). Predict y when x = 8.
items.e: Put x = 8 in: 2.5(8) + 10. So about 30 in..

items.q: The line of best fit is y = 5x + 60 (x = hours studied, y = test score). What does the y-intercept mean?
c: A student who studies 0 hours is predicted to score about 60
items.e: When x = 0, y = 60: a student who studies 0 hours is predicted to score about 60.

items.q: A line of best fit is y = −3x + 90, where x is days absent and y is grade. Predict y when x = 12.
items.e: Put x = 12 in: −3(12) + 90. So about 54 points.

items.q: The line of best fit is y = −3x + 90 (x = days absent, y = grade). What does the slope mean?
c: Each day absent raises the grade by 3
Each day absent lowers the grade by about 3 points
items.e: −3 is the change per day: each day absent lowers the grade by about 3 points.

items.q: A line of best fit is y = 0.5x + 2, where x is minutes and y is miles. Predict y when x = 30.
items.e: Put x = 30 in: 0.5(30) + 2. So about 17 mi.

items.q: The line of best fit is y = 12x + 15 (x = hours worked, y = pay ($)). What does the y-intercept mean?
c: About $15 is paid even for 0 hours (a base amount)
items.e: When x = 0, y = 15: about $15 is paid even for 0 hours (a base amount).

items.q: A line of best fit is y = 12x + 15, where x is hours worked and y is dollars. Predict y when x = 5.
items.e: Put x = 5 in: 12(5) + 15. So about 75 dollars.

items.q: The line of best fit is y = 0.8x + 1 (x = weeks, y = plant height (cm)). What does the slope mean?
c: The plant grows 1 cm each week
The plant grows about 0.8 cm each week
items.e: The plant grows about 0.8 cm each week.

items.q: A line of best fit is y = −1.5x + 40, where x is car age and y is value ($1,000s). Predict y when x = 10.
The line of best fit is y = −1.5x + 40 (x = car age (years), y = value ($1,000s)). What does the y-intercept mean?
c: A new car is worth about $40,000
items.e: At age 0 the value is 40 thousand: a new car is worth about $40,000.

items.q: A line of best fit is y = 4x + 30, where x is temperature over 60°F and y is drinks sold. Predict y when x = 9.
items.e: Put x = 9 in: 4(9) + 30. So about 66 drinks.

items.q: The line of best fit is y = 4x + 30 (x = degrees over 60°F, y = drinks sold). What does the slope mean?
c: About 4 more drinks are sold for each degree warmer
items.e: About 4 more drinks are sold for each degree warmer.

items.q: A line of best fit is y = 0.8x + 1, where x is weeks and y is plant height (cm). Predict y when x = 15.
items.e: Put x = 15 in: 0.8(15) + 1. So about 13 cm.

items.q: The line of best fit is y = 6x + 20 (x = people, y = party cost ($)). What does the y-intercept mean?
c: A $20 cost even with no people (like a room fee)
items.e: When x = 0, y = 20: a $20 cost even with no people (like a room fee).

items.q: A line of best fit is y = −2x + 75, where x is hours of TV a week and y is score. Predict y when x = 20.
items.e: Put x = 20 in: −2(20) + 75. So about 35 points.

items.q: The line of best fit is y = 2.5x + 10 (x = age (years), y = height (in.)). What does the slope mean?
c: Children grow about 2.5 in. per year in this data
Children are 2.5 in. tall at birth
items.e: Children grow about 2.5 in. per year in this data.

items.q: A line of best fit is y = 6x + 20, where x is people and y is cost ($). Predict y when x = 7.
items.e: Put x = 7 in: 6(7) + 20. So about 62 dollars.

items.q: The line of best fit is y = −2x + 75 (x = hours of TV a week, y = score). What does the slope mean?
c: Each extra hour of TV goes with about 2 fewer points
Each hour of TV adds 2 points
items.e: The slope shows a trend, not a cause: each extra hour of TV goes with about 2 fewer points.

items.q: A line of best fit predicts a score of 110 for 12 hours of study, but the test only goes to 100. What does this show?
c: Predictions far outside the data can be wrong
items.e: Predictions far outside the data can be wrong.

items.q: Which data would most likely show a negative association?
c: Hours of exercise and resting heart rate
items.e: More exercise tends to go with a lower resting heart rate: negative.

items.q: Which data would most likely show no association?
items.e: These are not related: shoe size and favorite number.

items.q: Which data would most likely show a positive association?
c: Number of rooms and price of a house
items.e: More rooms tend to go with a higher price: positive.

items.q: A scatter plot of x = hours of sleep and y = test score shows a positive association. Which is true?
c: Every student who sleeps more scores higher
Students who sleep more score lower
Students who sleep more tend to score higher
Sleep causes higher scores for sure
items.e: Association describes a tendency, not a rule or a cause: students who sleep more tend to score higher.

items.q: The points lie almost exactly on a straight line going down. How would you describe it?
items.e: Strong negative linear association.

items.q: The points go up but are widely spread. How would you describe it?
items.e: Weak positive association.

items.q: A line of best fit is y = 3x + 2. For which x is the predicted y equal to 20?
A line of best fit is y = −4x + 50. When does it predict y = 10?
A line of best fit passes through (2, 5) and (6, 13). What is its slope?
A line of best fit passes through (0, 4) and (5, 14). What is its equation?
items.e: Slope = 10 ÷ 5 = 2, intercept 4: y = 2x + 4.

items.q: A line of best fit passes through (0, 80) and (10, 30). What is its equation?
Why is it better to use a line of best fit than two random points to predict?
c: It uses the trend of all the data
items.e: It uses the trend of all the data.

items.q: A scatter plot of temperature and hot chocolate sales shows a negative association. Predict sales on a very cold day.
c: The same as a hot day
items.e: Colder (lower x) goes with more sales: high.

items.q: A scatter plot shows age and reading speed for children 6 to 12. Is it safe to use the line to predict for a 40-year-old?
c: Only if the slope is positive
No, 40 is far outside the data
items.e: No, 40 is far outside the data.

items.q: What is on each axis of a scatter plot?
items.e: One variable on each axis.

items.q: A cluster of points sits in the bottom left, and another in the top right. What might this mean?
c: There are two groups in the data
items.e: There are two groups in the data.

items.q: Removing an outlier usually makes the line of best fit …
items.e: It fits the other points better.

items.q: A line of best fit has slope 0. What does this suggest?
items.e: A flat trend means y does not change with x: no association.

items.q: Which is an example of bivariate data?
c: Number of pets in one house
items.e: Bivariate means two variables measured on each item: height and weight of 20 students.
